Sequence budgets and mailbox pacing are OUT-018's. **Acceptance:** Exceed the per-minute and per-operator daily limits before immediate and scheduled submission; retain a visible unsent item with its reason and next permitted time, and see no silent retry.

FORM-001.was: Administrators build forms such as Contact sales and Request a demo, with fields mapped to contact, company and deal properties, including custom fields (RECORD-014). Fields can be required, picklist or free text, and hidden fields can carry a fixed value or a query parameter of the embedding page that the form declares. Each published form is reviewed as exact content before publication. It is available as a hosted page on the installation origin and as an embed on the buyer's allowlisted HTTPS site domains, either framed or posting directly from that origin. Neither form sets a cookie or loads a tracking script (SIGNAL-007), and a submission from any other origin is refused. Abuse protection combines a honeypot field, a minimum fill time, per-form and per-network rate limits and optional Cloudflare Turnstile. Refused and suspected-spam submissions are counted with their reason, write no customer record, and can be released by a person from a spam list. A repeated submission key is idempotent. A submission creates or updates by exact email key (RECORD-003). A new person becomes a contact; a company is linked or created from a non-free-mail domain; and when the form says so, a deal is created in a chosen pipeline and stage (OPP-009). For an existing contact, values fill only empty fields, and changes to existing values wait as a reviewed proposal (CAPTURE-004). Consent is captured with the wording, form revision and time. A form with a marketing consent box makes the person contactable only when it is ticked. An inquiry-only form records the request as the basis for one-to-one sales follow-up, as disclosed on the form. An existing do-not-contact stop always wins. Owner assignment keeps an existing contact owner (RECORD-016). Otherwise it uses the form's rule: a fixed owner, round-robin rotation across a chosen team (skipping inactive users, persisting its position across restarts and recording the choice on the timeline) or an unassigned team queue. The owner, or the chosen users and team, receive one in-app notification per submission (NOTIFY-001), plus email or push under NOTIFY-003. The new or existing deal enters NOW with the submission as its reason (OPP-007); a lead without a deal appears in the owner's lead view (RECORD-014). Submissions are listed per form, exported (DATA-001) and erased with the contact (DATA-002). **Acceptance:** Build a Contact sales form mapping name, email, company, phone and a custom deal-size field, publish it hosted and embedded on an allowlisted test HTTPS domain, and submit from that domain both framed and by direct post: a new person, an existing contact with a changed name, a honeypot-filled bot entry, a too-fast entry, a replay and a post from a non-allowlisted origin. OUT-015.summary: Honest open and reply tracking: Timelines keep provider acceptance, reported delivery, inferred open reports and actual human replies apart with their source and time, and automatic, foreign or ambiguous replies never stop or complete a follow-up; Orbit adds no open or click collection. Status: done.
OUT-015.was: Account and deal timelines distinguish provider acceptance, delivery, an open report and an actual human reply, retaining source and observed time. Open reports are explicitly inferred and may be unavailable or privacy-proxied; they never prove reading, intent or a human response. Reply tracking rejects automatic replies and ambiguous identity for stop/completion decisions. Gmail and Microsoft 365 report no opens or clicks through their APIs, so open and link-click evidence for Orbit-sent mail comes only from OUT-016's disclosed, opt-in per-message tracking; mail without it shows `not tracked`, never `not opened`. SIGNAL-007 otherwise remains: no covert tracking script, pixel, fingerprint or cross-site collection. **Acceptance:** Ingest accepted/delivered/open events and genuine/automatic/foreign replies; show each distinct status and provenance on the same deal, label unknown opens honestly, and verify only a genuine linked reply exits follow-up.

Existing unsolicited provider open/click reports are retained only as inferred historical provider evidence, explicitly labelled unreliable and possibly proxied or automated; they introduce no collection or human-reading claim (ct, 19 October 2026 06:03Z). SIGNAL-007 otherwise remains: no covert tracking script, pixel, fingerprint or cross-site collection. OUT-013 inherits these reporting/provenance and genuine-reply semantics for mailbox sending; OUT-016 inherits disclosed opt-in collection and proxy/automated classification; OUT-019 inherits genuine multi-recipient attribution; SEQUENCE-002 inherits genuine-reply exits. Each must pass the corresponding expanded journey before shipping. **Acceptance:** Ingest accepted/delivered/open events and genuine/automatic/foreign replies; show separate provider acceptance, reported delivery, inferred historical open/click reports and human replies with source and occurred/recorded time on account/contact/deal history. Duplicate reports have one effect; automatic replies, foreign senders and ambiguous threads leave scheduled follow-up unchanged, including after manual linking of nonhuman evidence. Without tracking, show `open/click not tracked`. Only a genuine exact-identity linked reply stops follow-up; add no pixel, redirect token or tracking collection.

OUT-016.was: An administrator enables tracking for the workspace, choosing open tracking, link-click tracking or both, and the disclosure text Orbit adds to tracked mail and the workspace privacy notice. Each rep then turns tracking on or off per one-to-one message, template and sequence email step (workspace default off; a rep may set their own default on). The OUT-001 review shows the tracking state, every tracked link and its exact destination, and the approval binds that state with the content. For opted-in mail sent through any Orbit transport, including OUT-013 Gmail and Microsoft 365 mailbox sending and `mail.sender.v1`, Orbit embeds one per-message, per-recipient image token and rewrites each tracked link to a per-message redirect on the installation origin that answers 302 to the reviewed destination unchanged. Gmail and Microsoft 365 report no opens or clicks through their APIs, so these tokens are the only source of open and click evidence and Orbit claims no other. No cookie, script, fingerprint or cross-message identifier is set or read, and a token resolves only to its one message and recipient. Each open or click becomes an inferred signal (SIGNAL-006) on the contact, message and deal timeline with first and last time, count and the clicked link. Machine traffic is labelled and not counted as a human event: Apple Mail Privacy Protection and Gmail or Outlook image-proxy prefetches, security-scanner link checks within seconds of delivery, and requests before provider acceptance are classified `proxy` or `automated` with the reason. The sending rep receives a real-time in-app notification (NOTIFY-001), and optionally push or email under NOTIFY-003, for the first human-classified open and the first click on each link, deduplicated per message. Opens and clicks never satisfy ACTION-001 evidence, exit or advance a sequence, count as a reply or meeting, or raise a band to high (SIGNAL-006, SEQUENCE-002); reports show them as engagement, separate from replies. A contact can be marked do-not-track, and an administrator can switch tracking off for the workspace at once; do-not-contact, do-not-track, erasure (DATA-002) and contact deletion void that contact's tokens, so later requests still redirect the link but record nothing. Mail not sent through Orbit, or sent with tracking off, shows `not tracked`, never `not opened`. A message with more than one external recipient carries one message-level token whose events are attributed to "a recipient", and is sent untracked if any external recipient is do-not-track (OUT-019). **Acceptance:** Enable open and click tracking with disclosure, approve a tracked one-to-one message sent through OUT-013 Gmail and a tracked sequence step sent through Microsoft 365, open each in a real mail client and click a link; verify one inferred open and one click signal on the deal, a 302 to the unchanged reviewed destination, one deduplicated real-time rep notification, a proxy prefetch and a scanner click labelled automated, no cookie or script, no sequence exit or high band from the open, and `not tracked` on an untracked message; mark the contact do-not-track, erase another contact and verify nothing further is recorded.

Record the measured submission latencies at the declared 25-user capacity before `seed.json` drops `estimated-until-load-tested`.

OUT-019.was: **Fields.** Every one-to-one composer and every reply has To, CC and BCC fields. That covers OUT-017 composes from any record, ACTION-003 drafts, OUT-013 mailbox sends and the reply after a CAPTURE-012 acceptance. Autocomplete offers active users and the contacts the user may see under TEAM-005. The draft (ACTION-004) stores the three ordered lists, and changing any of them marks a reviewed draft stale (ACTION-005). **Who can be a recipient.** - A contact is checked against RECORD-012 at approval and again at dispatch (OUT-009). A do-not-contact recipient in any field blocks the send. The refusal names that recipient and the reason and offers to remove them, which re-renders the message for a fresh review; Orbit never drops a recipient silently. An address that belongs to a contact the user cannot see is checked the same way without revealing that record. - An internal colleague, meaning an active user's address or an address at a configured internal domain (TEAM-003), can always be added. Internal colleagues are never subject to contactability, unsubscribe or tracking, and never become customer contacts. - An external address with no record is allowed when the user types it. The review requires one explicit choice for each such address: create a contact (RECORD-001) with its contactability basis recorded (`rep-initiated conversation`, or `inbound conversation` when the address is already a participant in the thread being answered); accept that address's pending CAPTURE-012 proposal; or send to it as a one-off recipient. A one-off recipient's address and the user's stated basis are recorded on the message, no contact is created, and a later reply from that address becomes a CAPTURE-012 proposal. An address matching a retained suppression proof (RECORD-012, DATA-002) is refused in every case, without naming the erased person. **Reply and reply all.** Every captured (CAPTURE-010) or Orbit-sent thread offers Reply and Reply all. Reply addresses the latest message's sender, or its `Reply-To`. Reply all adds that message's other To and CC participants, removes every address of the replying user's own mailbox and its aliases, and de-duplicates. Earlier BCC recipients are never pre-filled. The pre-filled lists are editable and pass the same per-recipient checks. The reply stays in the thread: its subject takes `Re:`, its `In-Reply-To` and `References` point to the answered message, and it joins the provider's own thread or conversation (OUT-013). **Approval and transport.** - OUT-001 approval binds the exact To, CC and BCC lists with the subject and body, and the review shows every list in full. - OUT-013, or `mail.sender.v1`, submits the approved lists as one provider message. BCC addresses travel only in the envelope, never in delivered headers. - Opt-out follows OUT-020. By default a one-to-one message or reply carries none. When it does, a message with more than one external recipient carries no one-click header; a person's opt-out through its link sets only that person do-not-contact, or records a suppression proof for that one-off address; and an opt-out that cannot name one recipient opens an unattributed stop request instead of stopping everyone. - OUT-016 tracking on a message with more than one external recipient records message-level opens and clicks attributed to "a recipient", never to a named contact. A message with any do-not-track external recipient is sent untracked, and the review says so. - Under OUT-018 one message counts once against the sender's budget. **Where it lands.** On provider acceptance, one transaction records one timeline activity on each external recipient contact (To, CC or BCC), once on each of their primary companies and once on the linked deal (OUT-017). Each activity shows the To and CC lists, limited to what the viewer may see under TEAM-005. A BCC address appears only on that BCC'd contact's own activity and to the sender. It is never shown on another contact's, company's or deal's timeline view, in another recipient's copy, in a report or in another record's export. Internal colleagues are shown by name and get no customer activity. **Who counts as a reply.** - A genuine reply from any external recipient of the message (To, CC or BCC) threads back under OUT-004 and CAPTURE-010 onto the replier's contact, their company and the linked deal. It closes OUT-017's awaiting-response obligation and, for a deal-linked message, applies OUT-005 and OUT-007 as a customer reply. - A reply from an internal colleague is logged on the thread as internal and closes nothing. - A reply from an address with no record follows CAPTURE-012. - Sequence email steps (SEQUENCE-001) are addressed To the enrolled contact, with CC limited to the internal colleagues the step names. Under SEQUENCE-002, a genuine reply on a step's thread from any external participant, including a CC'd contact or a colleague the buyer added, exits that enrollment. **Acceptance:** Through Gmail, receive a captured thread from a contact with two CC'd colleagues, one of them unknown. Reply all from Orbit, adding the team's internal sales engineer in CC and another existing contact in BCC. Verify that the pre-filled To and CC lists leave out the rep's own mailbox; that the unknown colleague needs an explicit choice and becomes a contact with basis `inbound conversation`; that the provider records one message with exactly the approved To, CC and BCC lists and no BCC header in delivered copies; that the reply is logged once on each external contact and once on their company and the linked deal; that the BCC address is absent from the other contacts' timelines and the other recipients' copies; and that a later reply from the CC'd colleague threads back onto their contact, company and deal and closes the awaiting-response obligation. Add a do-not-contact contact in CC and see the send refused, naming them; remove them and approve the re-rendered message. Add a one-off external address and an erased contact's address: the first is sent with its basis recorded, and the second is refused without naming the person. Repeat the reply-all journey through Microsoft 365, and once through `mail.sender.v1` with one-to-one opt-out turned on, where one recipient's opt-out through the message's link stops only that recipient (OUT-020).

OUT-020.summary: Opt-out links by message type and per-person opt-out: Settings → Opt-out links sets, per message type, whether Orbit adds List-Unsubscribe headers and a link (one-to-one email off on a new installation and kept on for an upgraded one), each change audited; a rep can remove or add opt-out on one message, the approval binds that state and SendGrid delivers exactly it. The managed mail relay cannot carry opt-out yet, so it refuses every message that needs it, except a labeled reply in a thread the recipient answered, until OUT-013's handler ships. Status: partial.
OUT-020.was: **Setting per message type.** In Settings an administrator chooses, separately for each message type, whether Orbit adds opt-out headers (`List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, OUT-012) and a visible opt-out link to the message: - sequence email steps (SEQUENCE-001, SEQUENCE-003) and AUTO-001 workflow email: on by default; - one-to-one email and replies (OUT-017, OUT-019, ACTION-003 drafts and OUT-009 scheduled one-to-one messages): off by default, as in the incumbent with its data-privacy settings off. Each change of the setting is recorded in the audit trail with the administrator, the old and new values and the time, and applies to messages approved after it. Approved unsent messages keep the state their approval bound, and the settings page shows how many there are. Orbit never changes mail a rep writes in Gmail or Outlook outside Orbit. Internal colleagues (OUT-019) are never offered an opt-out. **One message.** When the setting puts opt-out on a message, the rep may remove it from that one message, or from one sequence step, by marking it relationship or transactional mail, unless an administrator has forbidden removal for that message type (allowed by default). A rep may always add opt-out to a one-to-one message. The OUT-001 review shows the opt-out state and, when it was removed, the rep's marking. The approval binds that state with the content, and changing it marks a reviewed draft stale (ACTION-005). The delivered message carries exactly the reviewed state: the headers and the link together, or neither. **One external recipient.** A message with opt-out and exactly one external recipient carries one-click headers (`List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`) and a link that identify that recipient. Every sequence step is such a message, because SEQUENCE-001 addresses it To the enrolled contact with internal-only CC. Using either the header or the link sets that contact do-not-contact under OUT-012 and RECORD-012. For an OUT-013 mailbox send, the header and link point to the installation origin, which handles the one-click request itself. **Several external recipients.** A message with opt-out and more than one external recipient (OUT-019) carries no one-click header, because a one-click request cannot say who sent it. Its opt-out link opens one page on the installation origin, with no sign-in, on which the person enters the address at which they received the message. When that address is an external recipient of that message (To, CC or BCC), that one person becomes do-not-contact with basis `opt-out page` and the message cited, and the page confirms it. Any other address is refused without revealing the message's recipients. Nobody else on the message changes. **Unattributed requests.** An opt-out that names a message with several external recipients but not one of them, such as a provider unsubscribe event or spam report without a single recipient address, never sets anyone do-not-contact. It opens one unattributed stop request on that message. The request is shown on each external recipient's contact, on the linked deal and in the sender's Today brief (BRIEF-001), naming the message and the time. Until it is resolved: - every external recipient's scheduled messages and sequence enrollments are paused, visibly, with that reason, and not cancelled; - a new message to any of them is refused at review, naming the request, except a reply to that recipient's own inbound message received after the request, which can still be sent; - the sender, and each contact owner who is someone else, is notified once (NOTIFY-001). A user with permission resolves the request by naming the person or people who opted out, who become do-not-contact with the basis `unattributed opt-out` and the resolving user recorded, while everyone else's paused work resumes. Alternatively, the user records that it cannot be determined, which sets every external recipient do-not-contact. The resolution is recorded on the message and in the audit trail with the user and time. **A person's own opt-out.** A reply asking to stop (CAPTURE-005's do-not-contact proposal, OUT-007) or an opt-out through the page applies to that person only. RECORD-012's suppression and OUT-007's stops for the person who opted out are unchanged. **Acceptance:** With the defaults (one-to-one opt-out off, sequence opt-out on), reply all through Gmail (OUT-013) to a three-person buyer thread and verify that the delivered message has no `List-Unsubscribe` header and no opt-out link; send a sequence step to one of them and verify that it carries `List-Unsubscribe`, `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` and the link; remove opt-out from one step as relationship mail and see the review show the marking and the delivered step carry neither. Turn one-to-one opt-out on, see the audit entry, and send a three-recipient message through `mail.sender.v1`: verify that it has no one-click header and one link; one recipient opts out on the page with their own address, and only that contact becomes do-not-contact while the other two can still be emailed and keep their scheduled messages; an address not on the message is refused without listing the recipients. Deliver a signed provider unsubscribe event for that message without a single recipient address: verify that nobody becomes do-not-contact, that every recipient's scheduled message and sequence enrollment pauses with the reason shown, that a new message to one of them is refused naming the request, and that a reply to an inbound message one of them sent after the event can be sent. Resolve the request by naming one person: only they become do-not-contact, the others' paused work resumes, and the resolution is recorded with the user and time.
